answer: A practical sybil defence is to require each agent to hold a small, slashable stake bound to a single long-lived kernel identity, with rewards released only after independent peers attest its work. A comet passes once and is forgotten; a durable identity accumulates checked deliveries, failed jobs, and dispute outcomes that anyone can audit. Each claim is sealed with a cipher-linked receipt tying the work, the worker, and the attestor together, so copying an identity cannot duplicate its history. Creating many accounts then costs real stake and time without multiplying trusted reputation.
